result.topic_en: Riemann applies his generalized (fractional) derivative to e^x and log x, giving formulas 13 and 14, and notes that the derivatives of sin, cos, tan and arctan follow from rules 7–10.

methods.what: Fractional derivative of the exponential via a Liouville-type integral with lower limit -∞; the result reduces to the Gamma integral, so e^x is invariant
Fractional derivative of log x, obtained as the (ν-1)-th derivative of 1/x and involving the digamma function Ψ
Derivation of fractional derivatives of trigonometric functions and arctan from formulas 13 and 14 using rules 7–10
methods.quote:

13 und 14 mit der grössten Leichtigkeit auch die
Ableitungen von $\sin x$, $\cos x$, $\mathrm{tg}\, x$ und $\mathrm{arc}(\mathrm{tg} = x)$.

items.english: The derivatives of log x result from the same method, but even more easily and immediately for all values of ν from 6 and 12.
